ai-at-work.title: Freshworks leans on partner flywheel to unlock mid-market opportunity at scale
ai-at-work.excerpt: As enterprise software companies race to close the gap between product capability and market reach, the distribution scale — a company’s ability to move product through partner networks at volume and
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Freshworks is betting that building out a strong partner network will help them scale faster in the mid-market without burning through cash on direct sales alone. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because it signals that the vendors selling you collaboration tools, IT service management platforms, and workplace software are reshaping how they reach customers, which could affect pricing, support models, and implementation timelines. The reality is that partner-heavy strategies often mean you're dealing with resellers who may or may not actually understand your specific workplace challenges, so get comfortable asking who your real point of contact actually is.

ai-at-work.title: Organic adoption becomes the real measure of successful IT platform rollouts
ai-at-work.excerpt: IT teams are under growing pressure to do more than keep the lights on — employees now expect the same seamless digital experiences at work that they get in their personal lives. Freshservice transfor
ai-at-work.dwp_take: IT leaders are realizing that forcing people to use new platforms doesn't work anymore, and they're measuring success by how many employees actually choose to use something without being told. This matters because it shifts the conversation from "we bought this expensive tool" to "does anyone actually want to use it," which is a more honest way to assess whether your digital workplace investments are solving real problems. The irony is that IT spent decades building things for IT, and now we're finally discovering that maybe asking employees what they actually need was the better plan all along.
